emergence.summary: Glycogen storage disease type II (acid maltase deficiency) -- the first lysosomal storage disease ever recognised. Loss-of-function of acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA), the lysosomal enzyme that hydrolyses glycogen to glucose, lowers lysosomal glycogen catabolism so glycogen ACCUMULATES in the lysosomes of cardiac and skeletal muscle -> hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and profound hypotonia in the infantile form; progressive limb-girdle and respiratory (diaphragm) weakness in the late-onset form. The catabolic throughput axis is driven DOWN; correction is to restore enzymatic throughput (replace the enzyme / stabilise the delivered enzyme) or to lower the upstream glycogen load. A lysosomal-storage read on the same level axis as Gaucher, A1AT-style level and Fabry -- but AUTOSOMAL recessive (17q25.3), a fourth storage read on a third enzyme that extends the storage class off the X chromosome. The kit re-derives the approved throughput-restore arms -- replace GAA (enzyme replacement: alglucosidase alfa, avalglucosidase alfa) + correct via a chaperone-stabilised co-dose (cipaglucosidase alfa + miglustat, where miglustat stabilises the recombinant enzyme so more active enzyme reaches the lysosome). The gamma read is of the GAA locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding/splice (e.g. the common late-onset leaky-splice IVS1 c.-32-13T>G allele), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

per_gene.note: GAA (acid alpha-glucosidase / acid maltase) is the lysosomal enzyme that hydrolyses lysosomal glycogen to glucose; LOF lowers glycogen catabolism -> glycogen accumulates in the lysosomes of cardiac and skeletal muscle (and diaphragm). Autosomal recessive (17q25.3). NCBI official symbol GAA. Coding/splice lesions (e.g. the common late-onset IVS1 c.-32-13T>G leaky-splice allele, c.525delT, p.Arg854X); promoter firewall respected.
per_gene.src: Hers 1963 Biochem J 86:11 (acid maltase deficiency, the first lysosomal storage disease); Kroos 2012 Hum Mutat 33:1161 (GAA mutation spectrum)
